At 2 o’clock on Friday afternoon Lee open ed a line of artillery fire from about one hun dred guns, concentrated against Cemetery Hill and the position along the cem. aeld by the second and a part of the first corps. The firing was responded to by all the batteries on the hill, and then ensued three hours of can nonading unsurpassed in incessant fierceness by any artillery battle on this continent.

Gen. Howard’s headquarters were in the cemetery, and were raked in a fearful man ner; men fell alt around him, but himself and staff escaped. The silent abode of the dead was made the theater of a deadly conflict. Tombstones and beautiful monuments were demolished; great holes were torn in the earth by the explosion of shells, and the rur face checkered with furrows.
